title: NASA and ESA facilities avoid major damage from wildfires in Spain
summary: NASA and ESA ground stations in Spain avoided significant damage from wildfires. The facilities are critical for space operations.

title: SpaceX conducts 13th Starship test flight
summary: SpaceX successfully launched its Starship on its 13th suborbital test flight on July 24, addressing issues from the previous attempt and deploying functioning satellites for the first time.

title: ULA deals with financial challenges caused by Vulcan grounding
summary: United Launch Alliance (ULA) secured a loan from its corporate parents to address financial challenges stemming from the grounding of its Vulcan Centaur rocket. The company is navigating these difficulties as it works to resolve the issues causing the rocket's suspension.

summary: LatConnect 60 introduced proprietary AI capabilities for its Earth observation satellites, responding to increased defense interest in the Indo-Pacific region for SWIRSAT.

title: Office of Space Commerce to move ahead on mission authorization
summary: The Commerce Department is advancing plans for a voluntary mission authorization system for new space activities not covered by existing regulations. This initiative aims to fill regulatory gaps in emerging space operations.

title: Lightning strikes Long March 3B after liftoff, Kinetica-1 launches 5 satellites
summary: A Long March 3B rocket successfully delivered its payload to orbit despite being struck by lightning shortly after liftoff. Separately, the Kinetica-1 rocket launched five satellites.
company: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC)

title: EU delays release of Copernicus imagery over Gulf of Oman
summary: The European Union delayed the release of Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 imagery for 24 hours after a U.S. request, citing concerns over the Gulf of Oman. The Copernicus program, managed by the EU, is affected by this temporary restriction.

title: Air Force takes over troubled military GPS receiver program
summary: The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center will now oversee the development, integration, and sustainment of military GPS receiver equipment. This move aims to address issues with the troubled program accessing the military’s encrypted GPS signal.
company: Air Force Life Cycle Management Center

title: NASA programs feel effects of workforce reductions
summary: NASA reports that over two dozen major projects have been impacted by a 20% reduction in its civil servant workforce over the past year. The workforce cuts are affecting critical programs across the agency.

title: Poland commits $745 million to EU’s IRIS² constellation project
summary: Poland has committed $745 million to the EU's IRIS² satellite internet constellation project. This investment supports the development of a multi-orbit satellite internet system.

title: What happened to space horror movies?
summary: Space horror movies have largely disappeared from production, with only a few exceptions in recent years. The decline may be due to shifting audience interests and the challenges of blending sci-fi horror effectively.

summary: Astronaut Michael Foale reflects on the 1997 Space Station Mir crisis, taking full responsibility for a collision while crediting the crew for saving the station. He shares insights on the incident and its aftermath.

summary: A new off-the-shelf camera could enhance the detection of black hole mergers without requiring new technology development. This innovation addresses an instrumentation challenge for LIGO.

summary: NASA astronaut Chris Williams and two Russian cosmonauts safely returned to Earth after spending 241 days aboard the International Space Station. The landing occurred early Sunday morning (July 26).

summary: The showrunners of 'Star Trek: Strange New Worlds' discuss their plans for season 4, including incorporating dinosaurs and Lovecraftian horrors into the series. They express enthusiasm for exploring these themes in the upcoming season.

summary: NASA's Juno probe has provided new insights into the subsurface of Jupiter's moon Io, revealing details about its volcanoes that could change how scientists study volcanic activity across the solar system, including Earth. The findings may transform understanding of volcanic processes.

title: Juno reveals surprising subsurface tempertures at Io, remarkably smooth surface
summary: Juno's recent flybys of Jupiter's moon Io revealed surprising subsurface temperatures and a remarkably smooth surface. The findings challenge previous assumptions about the volcanic moon's geology.

summary: NASA and Blue Origin have finalized plans to hot-fire test the second stage of the New Glenn rocket on the Stennis B-2 test stand. This marks a significant step in preparing the New Glenn rocket for its upcoming missions.

title: Starship Flight 13 achieves new firsts for SpaceX
summary: Starship Flight 13, featuring Booster 20 and Ship 40, achieved new milestones for SpaceX during its third attempt. The successful launch marks another step forward in SpaceX's development of the Starship program.

title: Soyuz MS-29 crew arrives at ISS, U.S. EVA completes Canadarm2 repairs
summary: The Soyuz MS-29 crew successfully arrived at the International Space Station (ISS), expanding the station's crew by three members. A U.S. extravehicular activity (EVA) completed repairs on the Canadarm2 robotic arm.

title: Path to Starship Flight 13 requires additional Booster 20 test
summary: SpaceX is preparing for Starship Flight 13, targeting a launch no earlier than July 23, but requires additional testing of Booster 20. The delay highlights ongoing technical challenges in the Starship program.

title: Falcon 9 to launch MRV-1 robotic servicing spacecraft for Northrop Grumman
summary: SpaceX's Falcon 9 is scheduled to launch the MRV-1 robotic servicing spacecraft for Northrop Grumman from Florida. This mission marks a significant step in robotic satellite servicing technology.

summary: SpaceX is preparing for a new attempt at launching Starship Flight 13 after a previous aborted launch. Additionally, Falcon 9 and Chinese rockets are also scheduled for upcoming launches.

summary: Relativity Space, Rocket Lab, and PLD Space are making progress on their new launch vehicles: Terran R, Neutron, and Miura 5, respectively. While Starship's test program has dominated recent attention, these companies continue advancing their heavy-lift rocket developments.

title: China’s first recovered booster returns to port as LandSpace aims for first land recovery
summary: China achieved a milestone with the recovery of its first booster, and LandSpace is now aiming for the first land-based recovery of a rocket stage.

title: Soyuz MS-29 launches new crew to ISS from Baikonur
summary: Soyuz MS-29 successfully launched a new crew to the International Space Station (ISS) from the Baikonur Cosmodrome. This marks another mission to maintain crew rotation and operations aboard the orbital laboratory.

summary: A breakthrough in robotic arm technology is highlighted as a significant advancement for space applications. The innovation is positioned as a potential game-changer for various space operations.

summary: The Proba-3 mission's Coronagraph spacecraft and its ASPIICS instrument are fully operational and ready to resume formation flying to create artificial eclipses. This marks a return to routine science operations after a successful health check.

summary: ESA's Prodex programme has enabled the successful launch of the 4DSpace-Daedalus mission in Norway. The programme supports research institutes in participating in European space science activities and missions.

summary: SpaceX successfully completed the 13th test flight of its Starship rocket, achieving the first intact water landing. The mission marks a significant milestone in the rocket's development.

summary: ESA has committed €65 million to support Europe's first lunar polar ice exploration rover mission, led by ispace-Europe. This marks a significant step in Europe's lunar exploration efforts.

summary: Lunar Outpost is planning to send NVIDIA chips to the Moon, highlighting the intersection of the semiconductor industry and lunar exploration efforts. This move underscores the growing importance of advanced computing technology in space missions.

title: A Deep Dive into the Bluetooth Satellite Connectivity Market Following the FCC’s Proposal
summary: The FCC is proposing to open unlicensed Bluetooth and Wi-Fi frequencies for space-based communications. This move could significantly impact the satellite connectivity market.

summary: FCC filings indicate Eutelsat is developing a new constellation of 528 satellites, separate from its OneWeb program. The company has not confirmed the full development status of this initiative.

summary: NASA has estimated a $2 billion cost for the Space Reactor-1 Freedom, a fission-powered spacecraft designed for interplanetary missions to Mars. This marks the first such mission powered by nuclear fission.

summary: The proposed Intel Authorization Act seeks to restrict commercial Earth observation (EO) satellite operators from sharing certain data with the public, framing EO data as a privilege rather than a right. This move aims to give the US government greater control over the dissemination of satellite imagery.

title: The UK Scraps the Department in Charge of UKSA

title: The UK and Space Florida Launch Joint Fund
summary: The UK and Space Florida have launched a joint fund to support projects with partners from both regions. This initiative aims to foster collaboration between the UK and Florida's space sectors.

summary: NASA and Blue Origin will collaborate on hot fire testing for the New Glenn rocket's second stage at NASA's Stennis Space Center in Mississippi. This partnership aims to advance the development of the New Glenn rocket.

summary: Two new Galileo satellites, SAT 33 and SAT 34, have entered service, enhancing Europe's satellite navigation system. The European Space Agency (ESA) announced their operational status, boosting the Galileo constellation's capabilities.

summary: Intellian has launched a new terminal for Iridium's GMDSS maritime safety service, utilizing the Iridium Certus 100 service. The terminal was announced on Thursday.

summary: Frequency Electronics reported $18 million in recent contract wins, including an $11 million award from an undisclosed major aerospace prime contractor for a proliferated satellite program.

summary: The FCC approved a new C-band auction to clear 160 MHz of the upper C-band spectrum, building on previous auctions. This move aims to further allocate spectrum for wireless services.

summary: Lite Coms secured a $22 million contract from an unnamed government and defense customer to provide satellite communications for operational readiness. The company specializes in integration and manufacturing of satellite communication solutions.
